description: Symbols over a logarithmic x scale and a sqrt y scale. The fourth differential fixture: the log axis exercises the tick algorithm's powers-and-multiples path, which is where a port most easily diverges. Two more log axes carry a **degenerate** base, which is a number a specification may write and upstream draws: the base reaches the ticks, the labels and `nice` and never the geometry, d3 transforming by the natural log whatever base was asked for. A base of 0 takes d3's integer branch, generates nothing there because `k < base` never runs, and falls back to linear ticks across the domain; a base of 0.5 takes the other branch and legitimately yields none. Both place their marks exactly where a base-10 scale would. A fourth log scale has a domain that touches zero, which really is unusable — every `scale(x)` on one answers null upstream — and upstream still draws the axis that names it, line and title and no ticks at all. Refusing to build the scale took the axis with it and called a chart upstream draws a defect in this engine.
